text: Why, ’tis no great matter; for a very little thief of occasion will rob you of a great deal of patience.
plain: Small annoyances steal your patience if you let them. Do not hand it over that cheap.

text:
We call a nettle but a nettle, and
The faults of fools but folly.
plain: Call a thing what it is. A nuisance is a nuisance and a mistake is a mistake.

text:
I had rather have my wounds to heal again
Than hear say how I got them.
plain: Do the work and skip the applause. Praise hurts more than the scars.

text:
I had rather have one scratch my head i’ th’ sun
When the alarum were struck than idly sit
To hear my nothings monstered.
plain: Better to be in the fight than to sit and listen to people inflate what you have done.

text:
I had rather be their servant in my way
Than sway with them in theirs.
plain: Better to serve on your own terms than to rule on someone else's.

text:
Despising
For you the city, thus I turn my back.
There is a world elsewhere.
plain: If this place does not want you, leave. The world is bigger than one room.

text:
You were used
To say extremities was the trier of spirits;
That common chances common men could bear;
That when the sea was calm, all boats alike
Showed mastership in floating; fortune’s blows
When most struck home, being gentle wounded craves
A noble cunning.
plain: Anyone can float in calm water. Hard blows test you, and taking them well takes skill.

text: I shall be loved when I am lacked.
plain: People only see what you were worth once you are gone.

text:
’Tis fond to wail inevitable strokes
As ’tis to laugh at ’em.
plain: It is foolish to cry over what cannot be avoided, and just as foolish to laugh it off.

text:
Anger’s my meat. I sup upon myself
And so shall starve with feeding.
plain: Living on anger means eating yourself alive. It never fills you.

text:
Now we have shown our power,
Let us seem humbler after it is done
Than when it was a-doing.
plain: After you win, act smaller than you did while you were fighting.

text:
Though thy tackle’s torn,
Thou show’st a noble vessel.
plain: Even broken and battered, you can still look like someone worth following.

text:
So our virtues
Lie in th’ interpretation of the time,
And power, unto itself most commendable,
Hath not a tomb so evident as a chair
T’ extol what it hath done.
plain: Your good name depends on the era judging it, and power's own praise is the loudest proof it is fading.

text:
One fire drives out one fire, one nail one nail;
Rights by rights falter; strengths by strengths do fail.
plain: A new force replaces an old one. Nothing holds just because it is strong now.

text:
Like a dull actor now,
I have forgot my part, and I am out,
Even to a full disgrace.
plain: The feeling of blanking in front of everyone. It happens to the best, and it passes.

text:
Think’st thou it honourable for a noble man
Still to remember wrongs?
plain: Holding on to every wrong done to you is not strength.

text:
He was not taken well; he had not dined.
The veins unfilled, our blood is cold, and then
We pout upon the morning, are unapt
To give or to forgive; but when we have stuffed
These pipes and these conveyances of our blood
With wine and feeding, we have suppler souls
Than in our priestlike fasts.
plain: A hungry, tired person is not at their best. Eat and rest before you judge or decide.

text: There is differency between a grub and a butterfly, yet your butterfly was a grub.
plain: People change completely. What you are now does not limit what you become.

text:
His nature is too noble for the world.
He would not flatter Neptune for his trident
Or Jove for’s power to thunder. His heart’s his mouth;
What his breast forges, that his tongue must vent,
And, being angry, does forget that ever
He heard the name of death.
plain: Honest to a fault. He will not flatter anyone and cannot hide his anger, and it costs him.

text:
I will not do’t,
Lest I surcease to honour mine own truth
And, by my body’s action, teach my mind
A most inherent baseness.
plain: What you do with your body trains your mind. Act small and you become small.

text:
I have a heart as little apt as yours,
But yet a brain that leads my use of anger
To better vantage.
plain: Same anger as you. I just aim it where it helps me.

text:
But now ’tis odds beyond arithmetic,
And manhood is called foolery when it stands
Against a falling fabric.
plain: Some fights are lost already. Standing alone against a collapse is not courage.

text: What is the city but the people?
plain: A place, a company, a country is only the people in it.

text:
Blessed be those,
How mean soe’er, that have their honest wills,
Which seasons comfort.
plain: Lucky are the people with simple wants. Getting what you want is what makes comfort sweet.

text:
I am senseless of your wrath; a touch more rare
Subdues all pangs, all fears.
plain: When something matters more to you than the threat, the fear goes quiet.

text:
The cloyed will—
That satiate yet unsatisfied desire, that tub
Both fill’d and running—ravening first the lamb,
Longs after for the garbage.
plain: A glutted appetite is never full. It eats the best and then craves the trash.

text:
Boldness be my friend!
Arm me, audacity, from head to foot!
plain: Walking into something scary? Ask for nerve and put it on like armor.

text:
Not any; but abide the change of time,
Quake in the present winter’s state, and wish
That warmer days would come.
plain: Some stretches you can only wait out. Shiver through the winter and keep wanting spring.
